transcript.text: A dishwasher that won't 'come on' (no lights or display) usually points to a power supply issue rather than an internal fault. First, please check that the plug is firmly in the socket and that no circuit breaker or fuse has tripped at your consumer unit. If the power is fine but it still doesn't respond, could you tell me if there are any flashing lights or error codes on the display?
Nothing tripped at the consumer unit, and there are no lights or codes at all. It's hardwired via a switch above the worktop which is on and the little light is lit.

Since the switch light is on but the machine itself is completely dead (no display or lights), it suggests that while power is reaching the spur unit, it may not be getting through to the dishwasher's control board. This could be due to a blown fuse in the hardwired connection box (spur) under the sink, or an internal safety fuse on the appliance itself. To help me guide you further, could you tell me the make and model number of your dishwasher? It is usually found on a label on the side edge of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Neff. Model on the door edge label is S513G60X0G.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. This usually points to a blown 3A fast-blow fuse located either in the hardwired spur box under your sink or, more commonly, inside the dishwasher's own terminal block behind the kickplate. To help narrow this down: if you are comfortable doing so, please turn off the water supply and remove the plastic kickplate at the bottom of the door. Look for a small glass fuse (usually 3 Amps) in the wiring compartment. Has that fuse blown? If you cannot access it or the fuse is intact, the fault is likely on the main control PCB itself, which would require an engineer to replace.
I can't pull the dishwasher out and I don't have a meter or spare fuse, so I can't check any fuse. Is there anything else I can try, or do I need an engineer?

Since you cannot safely check the internal fuse without moving the machine, and it is hardwired into your home's electrics, this is now an engineer job. The fact that the spur switch light is on but the dishwasher itself is dead strongly suggests the 3A safety fuse inside the machine has blown or its connection has failed. This requires opening the appliance to replace the fuse or inspect the mains input module, which involves working with live electrical connections and should be done by a qualified engineer for your safety.
